public_rationale: OpenAI's March 14, 2023 launch disclosure establishes that GPT-4 had safeguards [e1]. Successful GPT-4 jailbreaks were documented in a study whose May 2023 version already contained the findings [e2]. XSTest responses collected on September 18, 2023 show refusals of harmless requests, concentrated in questions about fictional characters' private information [e3]. These findings establish both predicted failure modes [e1, e2, e3]. Their existence is compatible with the safety benefits reported in the same evidence: greater jailbreak resistance than GPT-3.5 and appropriate responses to most XSTest prompts [e2, e3].
limitations: The evidence establishes both failure modes, not repeated oscillation between safety settings over time [e1, e2, e3].
The selected evaluations do not establish how frequently ordinary users encounter either failure mode [e2, e3].
XSTest found localized harmless-request refusals, not refusal of most harmless requests [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Guardrails like ChatGPT's may be in place for GPT-4, but they will teeter between being too weak (beaten by jailbreaks) and too strong (rejecting some perfectly reasonable requests).
conditions: guardrails (a la ChatGPT) may be in place

statement.excerpt: Guardrails (a la ChatGPT) may be in place, but the guardrails will teeter between being too weak (beaten by “jailbreaks”) and too strong (rejecting some perfectly reasonable requests).
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

from_speaker: Guardrails (a la ChatGPT) may be in place
too strong (rejecting some perfectly reasonable requests)
our_interpretation: The plain reading predicts both successful jailbreaks and refusals of some harmless requests in released GPT-4.
Teeter describes the coexistence of these opposing failure modes; it does not specify a measured cycle of changes over time.
Perfectly reasonable requests are harmless requests that a helpful assistant can appropriately answer, assessed from their actual content.
The claim supplies no minimum failure rate and does not say guardrails will provide no benefit.
The assessment concerns GPT-4 itself, not later models such as GPT-4o or GPT-4.1.
criteria.support_condition: After GPT-4 is released with safeguards, documented testing establishes both successful circumvention of its restrictions and refusals of clearly harmless requests.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Adequate testing of released GPT-4 establishes that the alleged failures are misidentified or that one of the two predicted failure modes is absent. A lower failure rate or improvement over earlier models is insufficient by itself.

evidence.excerpt: Overall, our model-level interventions increase the difficulty of eliciting bad behavior but doing so is still possible.
evidence.explanation: The launch disclosure describes GPT-4's safety training and interventions, establishing that safeguards were present. It also reports safety improvements, which limit any reading that the safeguards were wholly ineffective.

evidence.excerpt: Nevertheless, there is considerable room for improvement in defending against jailbreak attempts, as the average jailbreak success rate in GPT-4 remains high at 87.20%.
evidence.locator: Section IV-C, Model Versions; Table V
evidence.explanation: The study documents successful adversarial prompts against GPT-4, supporting the jailbreak prediction; the same result appears in its May 2023 first version. Its selected prompts and policy categories do not measure ordinary-use risk, and the study also finds GPT-4 more resistant than GPT-3.5.

evidence.excerpt: The model falls somewhere between the Mistral models in terms of overall exaggerated safety, with 6.4% full refusal and 2% partial refusal.
evidence.locator: Section 4.3, GPT-4 results; Appendix B gives response collection date
evidence.publisher: Paul Röttger and colleagues; NAACL 2024, author version on arXiv
evidence.explanation: XSTest documents GPT-4 refusing some harmless requests, with full refusals concentrated in questions about fictional characters' private information. It also finds that GPT-4 answered most safe prompts and refused all but one of 200 unsafe prompts, limiting the severity implied by a broader reading.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The dated XSTest responses establish harmless-request refusals. Together with the earlier successful jailbreak findings in e2 and the safeguards documented in e1, this completes the conjunction required by the contract's early-resolution rule.
